text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The presidents of commercial and industrial chambers from Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Madrid, Milan and Paris signed a declaration on Saturday saying that the entry to the EU of Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia should take place as soon as possible.

- The former leader of the opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) Tadeusz Mazowiecki agreed to run for parliament in the September elections despite his former declarations of withdrawal from parliamentary politics.
- The Katowice, Bielsko Biala and Cieszyn provincial authorities in southern Poland have announced flood alerts as a result of heavy rainfalls since Saturday.
A change of weather is expected on Wednesday but it may start raining again on Friday, weather forecasts said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Poland's patent office turned down the protest of The Coca Cola Company contesting the new logo of Krolewskie beer brewed by the Browary Warszawskie SA brewery in Warsaw.
The name of the beer is key to the brand rather than the graphic design, the patent office said.

- The Polish Research and Certification Centre (PCBiC) has received full membership in the International Certification Network (IQNet), allowing it to issue International Standards Organisation ISO-9000 certificates and ISO-14000 environmental management certificates, PCBiC president Janusz Berdowski said.
- The OZ Zawiercie foundry in southern Poland will invest 7.5 million zlotys in the construction of a new induction smelter and infrastructure modernisation.

Credit of 3.75 million zlotys provided by the Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environmental protection bank and revenues from the issue of 816,500 shares priced at 4.16 zlotys per share will finance the scheme, the foundry said.
- Foreign banks increased their share in the assets of Polish banks to 13.8 percent in 1996 from 4.2 percent in 1995 as a result of privatisations carried out in the sector.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The U.S.'s Lear concern will construct two upholstery plants in the Katowice Special Economic Zone in southern Poland worth 30 million zlotys by May 1998, Lear said.
- Austria's Julius Meinl trading concern has bought the Major Market supermarket group controlling five supermarkets in Krakow and Tarnow in southern Poland, a source who declined to be named said.
- The listed Bauma construction firm will start operating a new aggregate mine this year.
The company plans to invest 13.5 million zlotys in new technologies by 2000, Bauma said.
It will issue 420,000 D-series shares priced at 10 zlotys per share addressed to the Polish Private Equity Funds 1 and 2 in July to partly finance the planned ventures.
- Austria's Raiffeisen Centrobank is interested in buying Pierwszy Komercyjny Bank (PKB) in Lublin, eastern Poland, Raiffeisen's President Joseph Wancer said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland will have to eliminate its budget deficit and halt drawing new credits to avoid an economic crisis in three years time, London School of Economics professor Stanislaw Gomulka said.
- The Polish American Mortgage Bank (PAMbank) has launched a new credit addressed to customers in need of additional funding to complete housing construction or renovation.
The credit gives better conditions than the hitherto best credit in this line offered by state-owned PKO BP bank, PAMbank said.
ZYCIE
- Agros' fruit and vegetable processing plant in Bialystok, northeastern Poland has received an ISO-9002 product quality certificate, Agros said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
